$comment: The committed lift fixture (ADR J §4.1, §8.2). Both TypeScript repositories assert against it, so anatomy-dsl and design-system lift identically and cannot drift apart without a failing test.

`values` is the value lift this package implements: `liftSymbols(value)` over what the YAML parser holds for a style value — a scalar or a sequence of scalars — returning the symbols in fallback order. A primitive is not a symbol: it resolves against nothing by design, so it is never lifted.
`rejections` is the retired notation, with the rule each breaks. Every one throws an AnatomyValueError naming the value and the rule.

`names` is the CSS-name lift of §5.1 step 5d, which design-system implements because it needs S4 to run: a custom-property name to the dotted symbol it lifts to, or null where it names no symbol in any stratum and is kept as consumed with a register row (AT.09). It is DATA here, not an implementation — this package ships it so the two repositories agree on the expected pairs.

values.case: a camelCase segment is the symbol's own spelling, not renamed
a channel symbol, consumed by name where the implementation reads the channel
the programme's central binding: a channel then the semantic token
three ranks, in the reference's own order
a terminal literal is kept in the value and lifted from none of it
a bare keyword, for a key the registry says takes a primitive
a hyphenated CSS keyword, which the reference uses throughout
a literal holding a slash between spaces: the slash ban is on symbol spellings, never on literals
a literal a bare YAML would read as an alias
an undeclared name is still a symbol by grammar: whether it resolves is the register's question, not the parser's
a computed state variable, kept as consumed under the hover.X spelling

rejections.case: a slash path with a camelCase-bearing segment
a slash path inside a sequence
the retired optional marker on a slash path
the retired optional marker on a dotted symbol
the reserved root segment inside a dotted name
a primitive before the end: the sequence is the fallback order and a literal is what the chain ends in
a one-element sequence: a fallback order needs two

names.case: camelCase is restored from the kebab spelling S4 emits
the drift spelling S4 also emits for the same symbol
a channel with no base symbol: kept as consumed, register row X7
a state variant of a channel: register row X5
a computed state variable: the double dash lifts to a dot, register row X15
a component-local variable is followed through its :root definition and replaced by what it consumes
a component-local variable whose definition is itself a chain
an undeclared name: kept as consumed with a comment, register row X1
a composite typography slot no stratum declares
